\[
I_{\text{out}} = \begin{cases} 255 & H \in [H_1, H_2],\ S \in [S_1, S_2],\ V \in [V_1, V_2] \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(H, S, V\): Hue, saturation and value of the pixel
- \(H_1, H_2\): The hue range, which may wrap through 0
- \(S_1, S_2, V_1, V_2\): The saturation and value ranges

H, S and V are the hue in degrees and the saturation and value from 0 to 1, from Smith's hexcone model. The bounds count as inside, as in OpenCV's inRange. When H_1 is above H_2, the hue range wraps through 0 degrees. It then means H at least H_1 or H at most H_2, so 330 to 30 selects reds. Gray pixels have no real hue. Their hue is 0, which is red, so a saturation minimum above 0 keeps them out. The default ranges, reds with saturation and value of at least 40 % and 30 %, are PixelNexus's own starting point.
